title: Middle of the Linked List
spaceBreakdown:
- ListNode* slow: one pointer → O(1)
- ListNode* fast: one pointer → O(1)
- not counted: input list, returned node
approach: Use two pointers starting at the head: a slow pointer advancing one node per step and a fast pointer advancing two. When the fast pointer cannot advance further (it is null or its next is null), the slow pointer has landed on the middle. For odd lengths it stops on the unique middle; for even lengths, because fast moves two at a time and stops at null, slow ends on the second of the two middle nodes - exactly what the problem requires.
hints: Can the middle be located in a single pass without first counting the nodes or storing them? The list has between 1 and 100 nodes.
Use two pointers: slow advances one node per step, fast advances two. On [1,2,3,4,5], after one step slow=2 and fast=3; keep going while fast can still move two steps.

```
slow = head
fast = head
while fast is not null and fast.next is not null:
    slow = slow.next
    fast = fast.next.next
return slow
```

**Single node** - only one node exists
`Input: [1]` → `Expected: [1]`
⚠️ Bug: loop condition `while (fast->next->next)` dereferences a null pointer → crash

**Two nodes** - smallest even-length case
`Input: [1,2]` → `Expected: [2]`
⚠️ Bug: condition `while (fast->next && fast->next->next)` never enters the loop, returns slow=head=1 instead of 2

**Even length** - two middle nodes, must return the second
`Input: [1,2,3,4,5,6]` → `Expected: [4,5,6]`
⚠️ Bug: condition `while (fast->next && fast->next->next)` stops one step early, returns node 3 instead of node 4

**All equal values** - values do not affect pointer logic
`Input: [7,7,7,7,7]` → `Expected: [7,7,7]`
⚠️ Bug: comparing node values instead of positions to pick the middle returns the wrong node

followUps.q: How would you also detect a cycle while finding the middle?
followUps.a: Keep the same slow/fast pointers; if fast ever equals slow again after both have moved, a cycle exists and there is no well-defined middle. Otherwise the standard logic gives the middle. Time stays O(n), space O(1).

followUps.q: What if the list arrives as a stream too large to store?
followUps.a: Nothing changes - slow and fast only hold two node references at a time and traverse sequentially, so streaming input is handled identically. Time O(n), space O(1).

followUps.q: Return the k-th node from the end instead of the middle.
followUps.a: Advance fast k steps first, then move slow and fast together one step at a time until fast is null; slow is then k from the end. Time O(n), space O(1).
